<thought>Based on the NMR data, the compound has 8 carbons and 8 hydrogens (C₈H₈). The ¹H NMR shows a para‑disubstituted aromatic ring (four equivalent aromatic protons) and two aliphatic CH₂ groups that appear as coupled triplets (J ≈ 7 Hz), indicating a –CH₂‑CH₂‑ fragment attached to the ring. The ¹³C NMR supports this with two distinct aliphatic carbon signals (~43 ppm benzylic, ~39 ppm adjacent CH₂) and aromatic carbons consistent with a symmetric para‑substituted benzene. The simplest structure matching C₈H₈, a para‑disubstituted benzene, and a –CH₂‑CH₂‑ side chain is **para‑ethylbenzene** (ethylbenzene with the ethyl group at the para position relative to a hydrogen). Its SMILES is “c1ccc(cc1)CC”. This accounts for the observed aromatic AA′BB′ pattern, the two coupled aliphatic triplets, and the carbon chemical shifts.</thought>
<final_answer>c1ccc(cc1)CC</final_answer>
